name: Piper PA-34 Seneca
summary: Six-seat light piston twin derived from the Cherokee Six fuselage, widely used for multi-engine training, charter and personal travel.

wings: Low, tapered wing derived from the single-engine family
engines: Two flat-six engines in slim nacelles; counter-rotating props
Nacelles end near the wing trailing edge
fuselage: Long six-seat cabin with four side windows and a double rear door on the left
Short, blunt nose with baggage compartment
tail: Swept fin with a low-set stabilator — not a T-tail

tellTales: Low-wing piston twin with a long single-engine-style six-seat cabin
Low-set horizontal tail rather than a T-tail
Double rear door on the left side

confusedWith.howToTell: The Seminole has a T-tail and a shorter four-seat cabin; the Seneca has a low tail and a longer six-seat cabin.
The Baron has a longer, more pointed nose and a sleeker rounded fuselage; the Seneca's nose is short and blunt.
The DA42 is a slender composite twin with long thin wings and a T-tail; the Seneca is a metal twin with a low tail.
The Duchess is a short four-seat T-tail twin; the Seneca has a conventional low tail and a longer six-seat cabin.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
